h1: The 7 Best VTech Cordless Phones of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best VTech Cordless Phones: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven VTech cordless phones from single handsets to five-handset systems, compared on range, answering machine and accessibility.
summary: The VTech IS8151-5 is the best VTech cordless phone, a five-handset DECT 6.0 system with a 2300 ft listed range, Bluetooth, power backup and expansion to 12 handsets. The VG232-4 is the family set with four handsets and big buttons, and the VG208-5 keeps a corded base for outages. The VG231-5 adds five handsets for less, while the CS6719-2, VG232 and VG131-11 cover smaller needs.
intro: On a VTech phone the model number tells you more than the photograph. Two sets can look identical on a shelf and still differ in handset count, in whether the base records messages, and in whether anything works when the power goes out. Handset count and the answering machine are the two decisions that change daily life, so settle those before you look at range claims.

Our editors read the listings for seven VTech systems and ranked them on the Primea score, weighing handset count, range claim, answering machine, outage resilience and accessibility features. Prices appear as buckets. Several listings omit a feature entirely, and we treat silence as absence, which is how a careful buyer should read it too.

products.name: VTech IS8151-5 Super Long Range 5 Handset DECT 6.0 Cordless Phone for Home with Answering Machine, 2300 ft Range, Call Blocking, Bluetooth, Headset Jack, Power Backup, Intercom, Expandable to 12 HS
products.verdict: The feature-heavy system with range, Bluetooth and power backup.
products.description:
The IS8151-5 ships with five handsets, a listed 2300 ft range, Bluetooth, a headset jack, call blocking and power backup. It can be expanded to 12 handsets and includes an answering machine, in the $100 to $200 bucket. Power backup keeps the base alive during a short outage, which a standard cordless base cannot do.

It ranks first because no other VTech here lists power backup, Bluetooth and expansion together. The VG232-4 costs half as much and covers most families, so the IS8151-5 wins on feature depth, not value.

Buy it for large homes and small offices with many extensions. The caveats are the highest price bucket and that range depends on walls, so treat 2300 ft as a best case. Skip it if you only need one or two handsets.
products.idealFor: Large homes and small offices with many phones.
products.skipIf: You only need one or two handsets.

products.name: VTech Cordless Phone with 4 Handsets, Big Buttons, Large Backlit Display, Answering Machine, DECT 6.0, Whole-Home Coverage, Intercom, Easy to Use - VG232-4
products.verdict: Four handsets, big buttons and an answering machine at a fair price.
products.description:
The VG232-4 includes four handsets with big buttons, a large backlit display, an answering machine, whole-home coverage and an intercom on DECT 6.0, in the $50 to $100 bucket. Large buttons and a bright display make dialing easy for older family members, and the intercom lets you page a handset across the house.

It ranks second because it hits the sweet spot of handsets and features while staying in the lower price bucket. Against the VG231-5, it trades one handset for the answering machine, which most households want more.

Buy it for multi-room homes with several users. The caveats are that no Bluetooth is listed and no range figure is given. Skip it if you need Bluetooth or power backup, where the IS8151-5 is the answer.
products.skipIf: You need Bluetooth or power backup.

products.name: VTech VG208-5 DECT 6.0 5-Handset Corded/Cordless Phone System
products.verdict: A corded base with five cordless handsets for outage resilience.
products.description:
The VG208-5 is a DECT 6.0 system with five handsets and a corded and cordless hybrid design, meaning the base unit has a corded phone alongside the cordless handsets. It sits in the $100 to $200 bucket. A corded handset draws power from the phone line itself, so it can keep working when the electricity fails and cordless bases go quiet.

It ranks third because the corded base can keep working when a cordless-only system would go dark, which the VG231-5 cannot do. But no answering machine is listed, so it gives up a convenience for resilience.

Buy it for homes wanting a corded fallback, especially where outages are common. The caveats are the missing answering machine and the high price bucket. Skip it if you need built-in message recording.
products.skipIf: You need a built-in answering machine.

products.name: VTech DECT 6.0 Cordless Phone, 5-Handset, Interference-Free Sound, Large Backlit Display, Big Buttons, Caller ID - VG231-5
products.verdict: Five handsets with the accessibility basics, minus an answering machine.
products.description:
The VG231-5 includes five handsets, interference-free sound, a large backlit display, big buttons and caller ID on DECT 6.0, in the $50 to $100 bucket. Five handsets at the lower bucket is the draw: it puts a phone in every room for less than the VG208-5.

It lands fourth because it offers more handsets than the VG232-4 but omits the answering machine from its listed features. The VG208-5 does not list one either, but this model costs less and has the accessibility basics.

Buy it for large households wanting many extensions. The caveats are no answering machine and no Bluetooth. Skip it if you want a built-in recorder, because the VG232-4 gives you one.
products.skipIf: You want a built-in answering machine.

products.name: VTech CS6719-2 2-Handset Cordless Phone with Caller ID/Call Waiting, Handset Intercom & Backlit Display/Keypad, Silver
products.verdict: A plain two-handset phone with caller ID and call waiting.
products.description:
The CS6719-2 includes two handsets, caller ID and call waiting, a handset intercom and a backlit display and keypad, in silver, at $25 to $50. Call waiting shows who is ringing during a call, and the intercom works between the two handsets.

It ranks fifth because the bigger systems add more handsets and extras, but this one is the straightforward pick for a small home. It also costs less than any of the multi-handset sets above it.

Buy it for apartments needing two basic phones. The caveats are no answering machine listed and few extras. Skip it if you want a larger system, where the VG232-4 or VG231-5 scale up better.

products.name: VTech Cordless Home Phone with Answering Machine, Full-Duplex Speakerphone, Large Backlit Display, Big Buttons, Caller ID, Easy Setup - VG232
products.verdict: One handset with an answering machine and a proper speakerphone.
products.description:
The VG232 is a single-handset phone with an answering machine, a full-duplex speakerphone, a large backlit display, big buttons and caller ID, at $25 to $50. A full-duplex speaker lets both people talk freely, with no clipped words, which suits hands-free calls.

It ranks sixth because one handset limits flexibility, unlike the VG232-4 which pairs the same family features with four phones. For a single room, though, it delivers the answerer and speaker at a low price.

Buy it for a single room or an older relative. The caveat is limited coverage with only one handset. Skip it if you need several handsets, because adding them is not mentioned in the listing.
products.idealFor: A single room or an older relative.

products.name: VTech Cordless Phone with DECT 6.0, Full-Duplex Speakerphone, Lighted Display, Backlit Keypad, Caller ID/Call Waiting, Volume Control, Hearing Aid Compatible, Wall Mount - VG131-11 (Black)
products.verdict: The cheapest option, with wall mounting and hearing aid compatibility.
products.description:
The VG131-11 offers a full-duplex speakerphone, lighted display, backlit keypad, caller ID and call waiting, volume control, hearing aid compatibility and wall mounting, on DECT 6.0, in the under $25 bucket. Hearing aid compatibility means the earpiece reduces the interference that hearing aids otherwise pick up.

It ranks last only because it is the most basic of the group, with no answering machine listed. But it is the cheapest, and its wall mount fits a kitchen or workshop where a desk base would not.

Buy it for kitchens, or for users needing hearing aid compatibility. The caveat is the minimal features, so skip it if you want an answering machine or multiple handsets.
products.idealFor: Kitchens or users needing hearing aid compatibility.

whatMatters.detail: Handsets are the cordless phones that pair to the base. More handsets mean extensions in more rooms, but each costs money and charging space. Choose one per room you actually use, and confirm the number in the title, such as 4 or 5 Handsets, since some listings count the base as one. A phone in every room you use is the goal.

Range is how far a handset can roam from the base. VTech's IS8151-5 lists 2300 ft, but walls cut that sharply, and that is an open-air figure. Treat the number as a maximum, and favor systems that mention whole-home coverage if your house is large or has thick walls. Brick and concrete cut signal faster than drywall.

A built-in answering machine records messages in the base, with no carrier voicemail needed. It matters for homes without a voicemail plan. Look for the words answering machine in the title or bullets, and note that the VG208-5, VG231-5 and CS6719-2 listings do not mention one. If messages matter, buy a model that names the machine.

A cordless base needs mains power to run, so a plain set goes quiet in an outage. The VG208-5 has a corded base, and the IS8151-5 lists power backup. Check the listing if you want calls to work during outages, and keep a corded phone somewhere as a failsafe. A battery backup only covers a brief outage.

Big buttons, large backlit displays, volume control and hearing aid compatibility make a phone easier for older users. Check each feature by name, as the VG131-11 lists hearing aid compatibility and the VG232 lists a large display, and handle a phone before buying one for a relative. Fit matters as much as features.

faq.a: It is a cordless phone standard that uses its own radio band, which helps avoid WiFi interference. Every VTech here uses it, so the choice is about features and handsets. The standard is not what separates these phones.
Cordless bases need power. The IS8151-5 lists power backup, and the VG208-5 has a corded base, so those two are the best outage choices. A corded handset works even if the base loses power entirely.

faq.q: Is the IS8151-5 worth the extra cost?
faq.a: If you want Bluetooth, power backup or expansion to 12 handsets, yes. Otherwise the VG232-4 covers most homes for roughly half the cost. It adds big buttons and an answering machine as well.

Ignoring the answering machine. Several of these listings, including the VG231-5 and VG208-5, do not mention one, so confirm before buying. A phone without a recorder pushes you toward a paid voicemail plan.

Register extra handsets to the base following the manual. The IS8151-5 supports up to 12 handsets, while the other listings do not state a limit. Register each handset at the base, and label them by room.
The VG131-11 is listed as wall mountable, which makes it the pick for kitchens. The other models are designed for desk or counter bases. A wall mount frees counter space in small kitchens.

finalTake: Buy the IS8151-5 for a large home or small office that needs range, Bluetooth and a backup, and the VG232-4 for a typical family. The VG208-5 is the outage-resistant choice, and the VG231-5 is the five-handset value. The CS6719-2, VG232 and VG131-11 are for small spaces, single rooms and kitchens. Check which models include an answering machine, because several do not.
